title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a (topological, later differentiable) surface and x a point of X. D_x^* is the germ of the punctured disc around x (or a punctured neighbourhood), and U is an ambient open set. On the previous page Grothendieck attaches to each germ of arc γ: I=[0,ε) → X issuing from x a 'base point' for the punctured disc. Its lift to the punctured part gives a germ [I] → D_x^*. From this he forms the universal covering D_x^{*~}_γ := Revuniv(D_x^*, ([I], φ)), rigidified by a lift of the arc. He shows π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) = π_1(U,[I]), which receives a map K_x from the local monodromy T_x (≅ Z). Section D begins comparing this with a differentiable structure.

This page:
(i) Differentiable arcs. A germ of curve from x is called differentiable if its parametrisation is differentiable and its tangent map at the origin, (73) R → Tang_x(X), is injective, i.e. the derivative is nonzero. The image of R^+ is then a closed half-line in T_x X, called the demi-tangente (half-tangent) of the arc.
(ii) The local fundamental groupoid. Back in the purely topological case, he defines a groupoid Chemins(X,x):
- its objects are the germs of arcs issuing from x;
- Isom(γ,γ') := Isom_{D_x^*}(D_x^{*~}_γ, D_x^{*~}_{γ'}) (74), i.e. isomorphisms of the universal coverings of the punctured disc pointed respectively by γ and γ'.
Called the 'groupoïde fondamental local de X en x', it comes by construction with an equivalence (75) Chemins(X,x) → Revuniv(D_x^*), the groupoid of universal coverings of the punctured disc. Every vertex group is therefore ≅ π_1(D_x^*) ≅ Z (the local monodromy).

Purpose: arcs (germs of paths ending at the puncture) serve as 'tangential' base points for the local, and then global, fundamental groupoid of U = X − {x}. On the next page, in the differentiable case, he restricts to differentiable arcs (Germesrevdiff) and constructs an equivalence with Π_1(S_x), where S_x ≅ S^1 is the circle of half-lines in T_x X. On objects this equivalence sends an arc to its half-tangent. This is a topological/differential incarnation of tangential base points: arcs with the same half-tangent should be canonically isomorphic, and the groupoid of directions is the fundamental groupoid of the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up at x.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The equivalence (75) is tautological 'par construction', since morphisms are defined as isomorphisms of the pointed universal covers.
Minor imprecision: the 'tangent map R → Tang_x(X)' only makes sense on R^+ for a germ defined on [0,ε) (one-sided derivative). Injectivity just means a nonzero one-sided derivative.
The page does not justify that Isom(γ,γ') is nonempty (it is, since D_x^* is connected) or that the vertex groups are Z. Both are implicit and standard.

ideas.what: Half-tangent of a differentiable arc germ issuing from a point: the image of R^+ under the tangent map at the origin, assuming the derivative is nonzero
ideas.modern_name: direction / point of the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up; tangent direction of a tangential base point
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (differential geometry); the real oriented blow-up is associated with A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama in log geometry

ideas.what: Local fundamental groupoid at x whose objects are germs of arcs issuing from x and whose morphisms are isomorphisms of the correspondingly pointed universal covers of the punctured disc
ideas.modern_name: tangential (or 'path-germ') base points; local fundamental groupoid at a puncture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (tangential base points, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); also Ihara, Anderson; Grothendieck's own 'points base' discussion around the Esquisse and the Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Possibly in parts of La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) and in the spirit of the Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this continuation (pp. 650bis–787) is unpublished

ideas.what: Equivalence of the arc-groupoid with the groupoid of universal coverings of the punctured disc, and (next page) of the differentiable-arc groupoid with Π_1 of the circle of directions S_x
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points as points of the boundary circle of the real blow-up; Π_1(S^1) modelling local monodromy
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore after Deligne; made explicit in later work on tangential base points and real blow-ups (e.g. Nakamura, Kato–Nakayama)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines tangential base points purely topologically, as germs of arcs issuing from the puncture, organised into a 'local fundamental groupoid'. In the differentiable case he identifies this groupoid with Π_1 of the circle of half-tangent directions. This anticipates the now-standard picture of tangential base points as points of the boundary of the real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama space). It appears to be his own independent version, in the Longue Marche continuation, of Deligne's tangential base points.
missed.quote: nous allons considérer l'ensemble Chemins(X,x) des germes d'arcs de X issus de x, comme l'ensemble des objets d'un groupoïde (le groupoïde fondamental local de X en x)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it documents Grothendieck working out tangential base points in the Teichmüller/Galois context (≈1981, unpublished), close to or before Deligne's 1989 formalisation. Mathematically it is a clean arc-germ model of tangential base points, but it is not new to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a careful, essentially routine construction, but it is historically interesting: an unpublished Grothendieck treatment of tangential base points via germs of arcs and half-tangents, leading to Π_1 of the circle of directions. The idea itself is well known today (Deligne, real blow-up), so it is a modest surprise.
transcription_corrections: 'D^α' throughout is most likely D_x^* (punctured disc at x), consistent with the previous page's notation D_x^{*~}. So (74) reads Isom(γ,γ') := Isom_{D_x^*}(D^{*~}_{x,γ}, D^{*~}_{x,γ'}), and (75) reads Chemins(X,x) → Revuniv(D_x^*).
The struck-out text before (74) reads 'Revêtements(D_x^*, γ)' / 'Revuniv(D_x^*,γ)'. The target in (75) is likely 'Revuniv(D_x^*)' (cf. the diagram on the next page), not 'Revêtements(D^α)'.
'demi-droite homogène[?]' is uncertain. The word is perhaps 'fermée' or similar, describing a half-line in the tangent space.
The heading word is 'Chemins' (underlined in (75)), matching 'l'ensemble Chemins(X,x) des germes d'arcs'.
